A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same GILC paper, including Appendices A-D. Their text, equations, figures, and tables can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original GILC experiments on DNA, proteins, molecules, and images, including quantitative comparisons in Section 4 and ablations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including GILC results in Tables 1, 3, 4, and 6, generated image examples, and the Appendix D ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same variational proxy, Jacobian-free logit correction, GILC-DB and GILC-PG estimators, and Algorithms 1-3. Algorithm relocation does not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain HepG2 enhancer design, protein inverse folding and stability, QM9 property and fingerprint guidance, CIFAR-10 class conditioning, and Meissonic text-to-image aesthetic guidance.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1-4 and 6 is unchanged, including CG/CFG, DRAKES variants, Best-of-N, SMC, SVDD, and TFG-Flow where applicable. Newly cited CDD is discussed only as related work.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same splits, models, metrics, sampling procedures, and sample counts, including 640 DNA sequences and 4,096 molecules per property. The ESMFold citation repair does not change the evaluator or protocol.

E4.justification: The value-estimation, Jacobian, guidance-strength, and reward-call scheduling analyses are unchanged, including Figures 2-3, 5-7, and 10 and Tables 7-10. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 1, 3, and 4 continue to report means and standard deviations over three random seeds. The appendix uncertainty reporting and reported run information are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and generated examples are unchanged throughout both PDFs. For example, GILC-DB retains DNA Pred-Activity of 7.04 ± 0.26 in Table 1 and protein success rate of 82.4 ± 2.5% in Table 3.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, equations, and derivations in Sections 2-3 and Appendix B match after accounting for pagination. Neither the factorization derivation nor the logit-guidance equivalence proof is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and Section 5 retain the same claims about training-free guidance, differentiable and non-differentiable rewards, performance, and computational efficiency.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of experimental results, and stated limitations remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same concerns about Monte Carlo reward-query costs and the mean-field token-independence assumption.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same implementation details, model sources, hyperparameters, sampling budgets, and single NVIDIA A100 80 GB hardware disclosure. ESMFold was already identified and cited in Section 4.2; repairing its appendix citation adds no new implementation instructions.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds CDD (Cardei et al., 2026), describing its augmented-Lagrangian approach to hard constraints and positioning GILC's expected-reward gradient estimation as orthogonal. This is a limited extension of the related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short CDD discussion, replaces the unresolved ESMFold citation in Appendix C.3 with Lin et al. (2022), and adds the corresponding bibliography entries. The main exposition and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited bibliography and appendix reflow: Table 5 moves lower on page 14, and Algorithm 2 moves from page 16 to page 17. Figure and table content, captions, and visual designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The added CDD comparison clarifies GILC's relationship to another training-free approach, while the ESMFold citation repair removes an unresolved reference in Appendix C.3. These improve scholarly context and editorial completeness; the methods, theory, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
